titre.sous: will, be going to, present continuous

trois.kicker: Three ways to talk about the future

lignes.exemple: We **are going to launch** in May.

bulles.texte: No need. Tom **is going to fix** it after lunch.

q.entendu: Woman: We **are going to move** the launch to **June**.

etapes.texte: Listen for the **future form**: will, going to, is leaving
Catch the **time word**: tomorrow, next month, in June
The right answer says the __same plan__ in other words

phrases.texte: English has three common ways to talk about the future. Will is for a decision made now: I will call the supplier.
phrases.dit: English has three common ways to talk about the future. Will, is for a decision made now: I will call the supplier.

phrases.texte: Be going to is for a plan made before: we are going to launch in May.
phrases.dit: Be going to, is for a plan made before: we are going to launch in May.

phrases.texte: And the present continuous is for an arrangement with a fixed date or time: the train is leaving at six.
Listen to this example. The printer is broken. I will call the technician. It is a decision at this moment.
No need. Tom is going to fix it after lunch. That was already planned.
In a conversation, some words announce a plan: I have decided to. We are planning to.
And I am about to means very soon.
phrases.dit: And, I am about to, means very soon.

phrases.texte: Now, a TOEIC question from Part 3. A woman says: We are going to move the launch to June.
phrases.dit: Now, a TOEIC question from Part three. A woman says: We are going to move the launch to June.

phrases.texte: What does the woman say about the launch? A: It took place in May. B: It will be in June.
phrases.dit: What does the woman say about the launch? Answer A. It took place in May. Answer B. It will be in June.

phrases.texte: C: It is cancelled. D: She has not decided yet.
phrases.dit: Answer C. It is cancelled. Answer D. She has not decided yet.

phrases.texte: Going to means the plan is decided. So D is wrong. And she moves the launch: she does not cancel it.
phrases.dit: Going to, means the plan is decided. So D is wrong. And she moves the launch: she does not cancel it.

phrases.texte: A is in the past, with the wrong month.
B is correct. It says the same plan in other words: the launch will be in June.
Three steps. One: listen for the future form.
Two: catch the time word: tomorrow, next month, in June.
Three: the right answer says the same plan in other words.

phrases.dit: Now, practise with the questions below.
